title: Cross-region SLO drift & traffic-shaping retrospective
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-03-09 between 22:14 UTC and 23:02 UTC we observed a cross-region degradation that caused a sustained SLO miss for the hosted text-generation API. Symptoms included elevated p99 latency (baseline ~320ms -> peak ~1.1s), a spike in 5xx error rate (~0.05% -> 2.6%), and customer-visible increased tail latency across EU and NA regions. The root of the event was a combination of a recent autoscaler config change, a traffic-shaping rollback in the control-plane route weights, and a circuit-breaker threshold that was too permissive, which delayed failover protective actions. This ticket is the postmortem and consolidated follow-up actions.
timeline: 2026-03-09T22:14Z: Pager triggered by SRE for elevated error rate on /v1/generate in eu-west-1
2026-03-09T22:18Z: Incident commander confirmed p99 latency > 800ms and 5xx > 1%; traffic shifted from eu-west-1 to us-west-2 by smart-routing policy
2026-03-09T22:22Z: We observed queued requests and backpressure on the runtime pods in us-west-2; autoscaler had delayed scale-up due to recent change (minPool=3 -> 1 for short spikes)
2026-03-09T22:30Z: Circuit breaker for runtime instances did not trip until 22:37Z due to threshold misconfiguration (tripping at 10% error rate instead of 0.5%)
2026-03-09T22:38Z: Manual override set to reduce route weight to us-west-2 and re-enable EU-only traffic; emergency scale-up of dedicated pool initiated
2026-03-09T22:50Z: Traffic stabilizes but p99 remained elevated due to cached KV saturation; we enabled prefix-KV eviction and adjusted batch sizes
2026-03-09T23:02Z: Incident declared mitigated; post-incident monitoring in place until 2026-03-10T08:00Z
impact: SLOs impacted: availability SLA for hosted-generation endpoint (target 99.95% 5xx rate) was missed for a 48-minute window. Approximately 4.3% of requests in EU and 2.1% in NA experienced >1s tail latency. Customer impact: several high-volume customers reported increased latency; no data loss or confidentiality concerns. Estimated revenue-impact window: 48 minutes; small subset of production traffic rerouted and saw degraded quality-of-service.
root_cause: Multiple contributing changes aligned: (1) autoscaler configuration change deployed 2026-03-07 reduced min pool size to reduce cost; under cross-region failover this produced insufficient spare capacity for burst; (2) control-plane rollback of a traffic-weighting adjustment caused excess routing to a partially loaded region; (3) circuit-breaker parameterization was set conservatively high by a recent tuning PR (trips at 10% errors) delaying protective shedding; and (4) runtime KV cache experienced fragmentation under uneven load causing longer KV lookups and increased tail latencies. The immediate trigger was the traffic-weighting rollback + inadequate autoscaler floor which caused queueing and resource exhaustion in the target region.
contributing_factors: Recent autoscaler change aimed at cost reduction (minPool=1) reduced headroom for failover
Control-plane route weights rollback during a separate deployment led to misrouted traffic
Circuit-breaker thresholds tuned for a different workload resulted in late tripping
KV cache fragmentation under bursty multi-tenant traffic increased per-request work
Lack of an automated pre-failover capacity check in smart-routing policy
mitigation: Rolled back autoscaler minPool to 3 for the affected pools (immediate revert)
Adjusted control-plane weights to restore EU prioritization and limited cross-region bursting
Manual lowering of circuit-breaker trip threshold to 0.5% to protect downstream services
Enabled aggressive KV cache eviction for hot prefixes and temporarily reduced batch size to lower per-request CPU
Opened customer incident communications for top 5 affected accounts with timeline and remediation steps
action_items: ENG-9482: Implement pre-failover capacity check in smart-routing (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-03-28)
ENG-9490: Create automated guardrail to prevent autoscaler minPool reductions below safety floor for multi-region pools (owner: Marco Liu, due: 2026-03-21)
ENG-9496: Revisit circuit-breaker defaults and add workload-aware profiles; add canary tests (owner: Diego Morales, due: 2026-04-02)
ENG-9501: Add KV cache fragmentation metrics and an alert when per-request KV latency > 150ms at 99th percentile (owner: SRE team, due: 2026-03-24)
ENG-9508: Post-deployment runbook update to include 'verify route weights' gate for control-plane rollbacks (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2026-03-18)
ENG-9515: Run a simulated multi-region failover load test weekly against staging with current autoscaler settings (owner: Reliability WG, due: 2026-03-31)
ENG-9522: Dashboard: add cross-region headroom metric and alert when headroom < 20% for any region (owner: Observability team, due: 2026-03-20)
followups: Weekly review of simulated failover tests in Reliability WG for 90 days
Plan a postmortem review with Product and Console teams to ensure customers can see per-region headroom in the Console
Schedule a tabletop incident review with SRE, Serving Runtime, and Control Plane engineers to walk through decision points
Track customer follow-ups for affected accounts and validate satisfaction after fixes
